strengths: First-of-its-kind extension of the highly popular and successful functional maps framework from 2D surfaces to 3D volumetric domains (specifically, tetrahedral meshes).
Mathematically sound formulation, particularly the insightful utilization of Neumann boundary conditions to properly handle boundary traces of the volumetric Laplace-Beltrami operator.

Demonstration of diverse and highly practical downstream applications, such as volumetric connectivity transfer, coordinate extrapolation, medical segmentation transfer, and bootstrapping existing mesh untangling algorithms (achieving an 85% success rate on previous state-of-the-art failure cases).
Rigorous experimental validation demonstrating that incorporating volumetric spectral information consistently improves shape matching accuracy, even for surface-to-surface correspondence tasks.
Excellent clarity of writing, well-designed figures, and a thorough appendix detailing algorithmic pseudocode, spectral properties under Weyl's law, and dataset limitations.
weaknesses: High computational overhead: Eigendecomposition and basis alignment on dense tetrahedral meshes introduce a notable slowdown (up to 2.5x as shown in Table 2) compared to surface-only methods.

Dependency on tetrahedralization quality: Generating high-quality tetrahedral meshes from raw, noisy, or non-manifold surface scans is a known bottleneck. Any topological alterations introduced during automatic tetrahedralization (e.g., via fTetWild) directly degrade the performance of the LBO eigenbasis.

Limited native volumetric evaluation: While the brain segmentation transfer task is compelling, the majority of the quantitative evaluations are performed on tetrahedralized surface benchmarks rather than natively acquired 3D volumetric datasets (e.g., raw clinical MRI/CT volumes or CAD solid models).

strengths: First complete extension of the functional maps framework to volumetric domains (tetrahedral meshes), opening up a new direction for spectral geometry processing.
Comprehensive theoretical and empirical validation, particularly regarding the properties of volumetric Laplace-Beltrami Operator (LBO) eigenfunctions, boundary traces, and isometric distortions.
Excellent practical utility demonstrated by boosting the success rate of state-of-the-art volumetric mesh untangling algorithms, resolving 85% of prior failure cases.
Insightful application to volume-aware surface matching, showing that incorporating volumetric information consistently improves surface correspondences over surface-only methods.
High-quality writing, clear illustrations, and complete algorithmic details (including pseudocode in the appendix) which ensure reproducibility.
weaknesses: Significant computational overhead due to the addition of internal vertices, resulting in slower eigendecomposition and alignment times compared to surface-only methods.

Strong dependence on the quality and topology of the volumetric discretization (tetrahedralization); topological noise introduced during volume meshing can negatively affect the LBO spectrum unless heavily regularized.

Evaluation on volumetric datasets is somewhat limited in scale (mainly utilizing the 40 pairs from Su et al.), although this is largely due to the scarcity of high-quality volumetric benchmarks in the community.

strengths: First systematic extension of the popular functional maps framework to 3D volumetric domains (tetrahedral meshes).

Thorough theoretical and empirical validation, demonstrating that the boundary restriction (traces) of volume LBO eigenfunctions form an expressive basis for surface signals under Neumann boundary conditions.

Showcases a variety of highly practical applications, such as bootstrapping volumetric mesh untangling (improving success rates from 0% to 85% on known difficult failure cases), segmentation transfer, and solid texturing.
Consistently improves surface-to-surface shape matching accuracy across multiple standard benchmarks (SHREC'19, SHREC'20, TOPKIDS) by incorporating volumetric information.
weaknesses: High computational overhead: Computing the volumetric LBO and aligning larger bases scales with the number of interior tetrahedral vertices, resulting in a 1x to 2.5x slowdown compared to surface-only methods.

Strong dependency on the quality of the tetrahedralization preprocessing step. If tools like fTetWild introduce topological artifacts (e.g., closing handles), the quality of the resulting volumetric eigenfunctions is degraded.

The core functional map estimation relies heavily on existing surface-based frameworks (like ZoomOut and Orthoprods) directly ported to the volumetric LBO, with limited algorithmic novelty in the map optimization itself.
